nodes.body: I just found issue https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/127335 which seems to be one cause for some of the randomly failing webhook invocations we see. Not that this issue here is not valid, there can always be network issues or crashes of processes.

without looking into much detail into all this issue, I can see these are POST requests

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/9d2fc46556af162ff42a4773349d0f92f9ef8d50/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/admission/plugin/webhook/validating/dispatcher.go#L283

and retrying POST request is usually unsafe, since you don't know if some write operation succeeded

> without looking into much detail into all this issue, I can see these are POST requests
> 
> https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/9d2fc46556af162ff42a4773349d0f92f9ef8d50/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/admission/plugin/webhook/validating/dispatcher.go#L283
> 
> and retrying POST request is usually unsafe, since you don't know if some write operation succeeded

The retrying (or the fact that 4xx indicates to the client that it or its data is at fault) was just an example of how the wrong status code could be interpreted. 

On a server error (5xx), which I am saying should be used here, it's usually safe for the client to try again.
Even more so, knowing we are talking about stateless webook invocations.

Thinking more about this, returning ANY valid HTTP status code is likely not the proper way if there was no HTTP communication (connection refused, EOF, ...). Certainly the HTTP call from the client (kubectl) maps the failure to reach the webhook to 500 anyway, but looking at e.g. the metrics or logs ... there should be a proper error handling mentioning that there was a connection issue, not some random HTTP code mapping.

There is a similar issue regarding etcd errors https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/112152

@aaron-prindle just accepted that one from triage.
/sig api-machinery
@kubernetes/sig-api-machinery-misc

I agree this should be 5xx.

EDIT: But switching to where we categorize errors too many failures as 500 (when some of them should have been 4xx) would also be wrong

### What happened?

kubectl get hpa incorrectly appends m (millicores) to memory usage values. Memory should always be displayed in bytes, MiB, or GiB, never in "millibytes (m)". This issue also exists in the autoscaling/v2 API, suggesting a deeper problem beyond kubectl

 Affected Versions
Kubernetes Version: v1.29+
kubectl Version: v1.29+
Metrics Server: latest stable
Environment: Affects both on-prem and cloud-managed Kubernetes (e.g., AKS, EKS, GKE).

Deploy an HPA that scales based on memory usage:

yaml

apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: test-hpa
  namespace: default
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: test-deployment
  minReplicas: 1
  maxReplicas: 10
  metrics:
    - type: Resource
      resource:
        name: memory
        target:
          type: AverageValue
          averageValue: 325Mi
Apply the configuration:

sh

kubectl apply -f test-hpa.yaml
Check HPA details:

sh

kubectl get hpa test-hpa -n default
Observed Output:

bash

NAME      REFERENCE        TARGETS      MINPODS   MAXPODS   REPLICAS   AGE
test-hpa  Deployment/test  171502796800m/325Mi   1         10        2          10m
Problem: The value 171502796800m should not have m, as memory is measured in bytes.

Fetch raw API data:

kubectl get --raw "/apis/autoscaling/v2/namespaces/default/horizontalpodautoscalers/test-hpa" | jq
API Output (Incorrect format):

json
{
  "status": {
    "currentMetrics": [
      {
        "type": "Resource",
        "resource": {
          "name": "memory",
          "current": {
            "averageValue": "**172043468800m**"
          }
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
🚨 Incorrect: The API also appends m, suggesting the issue is deeper than kubectl.


### What did you expect to happen?

Expected Behavior **Actual Behavior ( kubectl get hpa )
Memory should be displayed in MiB, GiB, or raw
bytes
Memory is displayed with an incorrect m suffix
Example: 171502796800 bytes = 163,599 MiB Shown incorrectly as 171502796800m
Consistent with Kubernetes documentation Misleading as "millibytes" (which is not a Kubernetes
unit)

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

refer

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

### Kubernetes version

 kubectl version
Client Version: v1.31.0
Kustomize Version: v5.4.2
Server Version: v1.29.10
WARNING: version difference between client (1.31) and server (1.29) exceeds the supported minor version skew of +/-1

title: Commit b31e779 added a blocker to dead code elimination by the Go compiler
body:
### What happened?

Commit b31e779 by @p0lyn0mial uses `cmp.Diff()` which depends on `reflect.Type.Method(n int)`. Upon encountering the use of this method, the go compiler disables the dead code elimination.

The commit message for b31e779 indicates that 
> The consistency check is meant to be enforced only in the CI, not in production.

Please fix the consistency check to disable the DCE only in CI, not in the production.

### What did you expect to happen?

Debug code must not pessimise the code generation for prod environments.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

You can use `go build -ldflags '-dumpdep'` to have the compiler dump the dependency graph of linked symbols. Any symbol marked with `<ReflectMethod>` disables the DCE.

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

### Kubernetes version

b31e7793d0d873a71c90caf8455556aa905cf88d

### Cloud provider

any

### OS version

_No response_

_No response_

nodes.body: /sig api-machinery

/cc @p0lyn0mial do you mind taking a look since this is introduced by your change? Thanks!

/triage accepted

Sure, I can take a look, though I’m not entirely sure what is expected here. 

I could modify the code to use [apiequality.Semantic.DeepEqual](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/a4819996a860066dfba5383e4fb6db2a243ad03e/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/third_party/forked/golang/reflect/deep_equal.go#L272) instead, but I’m not sure if that would help, as that function also relies on reflection. 

Perhaps we should consider using custom build tags specifically for CI.
It is an ok solution to have the debug code behind a build tag that you set only in CI builds.

> I could modify the code to use [apiequality.Semantic.DeepEqual](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/a4819996a860066dfba5383e4fb6db2a243ad03e/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/third_party/forked/golang/reflect/deep_equal.go#L272) instead, but I’m not sure if that would help, as that function also relies on reflection.

Using reflection is not an issue in itself, only using the `Method` or `MethodByName` methods of `reflect.Type` (or `reflect.Value`) with a non-constant argument disables the optimization, and I believe `apiequality.Semantic.DeepEqual` doesn't use those.
closing please see https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/132216

title: apiserver healthz should check etcd override endpoints
body:
### What happened?

It seems the apiserver will fail bootstrap if the etcd override endpoint is not healthy.
But after the bootstrap completes, if the etcd override endpoint become unhealthy, the apiserver health check will still report OK while `kubectl get cs` will report etcd override endpoint is not healthy.

### What did you expect to happen?

APIserver health check should report unhealthy when an etcd override endpoint is unhealthy.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Run 2 etcd clusters: one for events and one for the other resources. Then configure apiserver to use the event etcd using the `--etcd-servers-overrides` flag. After the apiserver complete the bootstrap, kill the event etcd.
You will be able to see APIServer health check still reporting OK.

title: DRA: Pod termination is stuck when DRA Driver is stopped
body:
### What happened?

A status of Pod allocated some device remains as terminating when the DRA Driver is stopped.
I don't know this is intentional or a bug.

### What did you expect to happen?

A Pod is completely terminated.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

We can reproduce it using [dra-example-driver](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/dra-example-driver).

### Summary
1. Install the `DRA Driver`(dra-example-driver) and create a `DeviceClass`.
1. Create a `ResourceClaimTemplate`.
1. Deploy a Pod allocated some device via the `ResourceClaimTemplate`.
1. Stop the DRA Driver.
1. Delete the Pod.
1. The Pod remains as terminating.

### Procedure

<details>

Install the `DRA Driver` and create a `DeviceClass` by following [dra-example-driver demo](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/dra-example-driver?tab=readme-ov-file#demo).

Create a `ResourceClaimTemplate`.

`resource-claim-template-0.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: resource.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: ResourceClaimTemplate
metadata:
  name: single-gpu
spec:
  spec:
    devices:
      requests:
      - name: gpu
        deviceClassName: gpu.example.com
```
```bash
$ kubectl apply -f resource-claim-template-0.yaml
```

Deploy a Pod allocated some device via the `ResourceClaimTemplate`.

`sample-pod-0.yaml`
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: sample-pod-0
  labels:
    app: sample-pod-0
spec:
  containers:
  - name: ctr0
    image: ubuntu:22.04
    command: ["bash", "-c"]
    args: ["export; trap 'exit 0' TERM; sleep 9999 & wait"]
    resources:
      claims:
      - name: gpu
  resourceClaims:
  - name: gpu
    resourceClaimTemplateName: single-gpu
```

```bash
$ kubectl apply -f sample-pod-0.yaml
```


The current status of cluster is as follows.
```bash
$ kubectl get deviceclasses,resourceclaimtemplates,resourceclaim,pods
NAME                                          AGE
deviceclass.resource.k8s.io/gpu.example.com   54m

NAME               READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
pod/sample-pod-0   1/1     Running   0          77s
```

Stop the DRA Driver.
In this case, we can uninstall the `dra-example-driver` via helm.
```bash
$ helm -n dra-example-driver uninstall dra-example-driver
```

Delete the Pod and the status remains as terminating.
```bash
$ kubectl delete po sample-pod-0
pod "sample-pod-0" deleted
(stucking...)

$ kubectl get pod
NAME           READY   STATUS        RESTARTS   AGE
sample-pod-0   0/1     Terminating   0          17m
```

This is probably the way it works, because when the pod is deleted, the kubelet needs to call dra-driver to call NodeUnprepareResource.
This is indeed intentional. The kubelet cannot distinguish between "DRA driver is permanently gone" and "only temporarily not available" and has to assume the latter.
@pohly do we have documentation or anything that states that this is a known behavior?

I'm not sure. Looking at https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-node/4381-dra-structured-parameters#kubelet, explanations about when exactly the kubelet calls DRA drivers are missing.

cc @bart0sh and @klueska - they know this part better than me, they implemented it.

I take that back. "Managing resources" has one paragraph about this:

> If this was the last Pod on the node that uses the specific resource instance, then NodeUnprepareResource (see below) must have been called successfully before allowing the pod to be deleted. This ensures that network-attached resource are available again for other Pods, including those that might get scheduled to other nodes. It also signals that it is safe to deallocate and delete the ResourceClaim.

TBH this may be a concerning bug for upgrades.

Let's say someone upgrades a node and they drain the nodes. If the dra driver is stopped before any pod that is using a resource claim then I guess that all these pods would be stuck in terminating?

This is not a bug, as it is working as designed. That said, I can see how it might raise eyebrows. I guess the alternative would be to have the kubelet allow  immediate deletion of the pod, but somehow track that there was still an outstanding claim to unprepared (and do so in a way that survives kubelet restarts / node reboots).

> Let's say someone upgrades a node and they drain the nodes. If the dra driver is stopped before any pod that is using a resource claim then I guess that all these pods would be stuck in terminating?

Isn't that handled by not stopping daemon set pods during a node drain?

> I guess the alternative would be to have the kubelet allow immediate deletion of the pod, but somehow track that there was still an outstanding claim to unprepared (and do so in a way that survives kubelet restarts / node reboots).

This breaks the "It also signals that it is safe to deallocate and delete the ResourceClaim." part. The rest of the system won't know that `NodeUnprepareResources` hasn't been completed yet.

> Let's say someone upgrades a node and they drain the nodes. If the dra driver is stopped before any pod that is using a resource claim then I guess that all these pods would be stuck in terminating?

This is the same behavior as with network plugins, if the CNI plugin does not respond the`CNI DEL` the Pod can not be deleted, so the network plugin must be the last to be stopped ... I agree with Kevin and Patrick that this is WAI, drivers should deallocate the resources for a safe shutdown and operators should have this in mind when deploying and managing the drivers
I guess then that is what we have. So the outcome is that if a dra driver is stopped it must be the last to be stopped.

> I guess then that is what we have. So the outcome is that if a dra driver is stopped it must be the last to be stopped.

we need a good shutdown history for the kubelet that makes these things invisible to users and allow developers to implement this functionality easily
So what would be the expectation if someone needs to update a DRA Driver? I guess that there could be a temporary issue where pods will be stuck in terminating until the DRA driver is ready again?
See https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/128964

> we need a good shutdown history for the kubelet that makes these things invisible to users and allow developers to implement this functionality easily

I haven't tried it for DRA, but https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/administer-cluster/safely-drain-node/ specifically talks about daemon sets.

> I guess the alternative would be to have the kubelet allow immediate deletion of the pod, but somehow track that there was still an outstanding claim to unprepared (and do so in a way that survives kubelet restarts / node reboots).

I think the CSI driver takes a similar approach when managing the mounting and unmounting of PVs on Nodes. The AttachDetach controller tracks the volume's mount state asynchronously via VolumeAttachment, allowing the Pod to terminate immediately. However, if the CSI driver’s Pod doesn’t stop after the Pod using the PV, the volume cleanup may not complete. This can leave orphaned VolumeAttachments, leading to multi-attach errors and preventing the Pod from starting on another Node, which causes issues.

> This can leave orphaned VolumeAttachments, leading to multi-attach errors and preventing the Pod from starting on another Node, which causes issues.

This is one of those problems that I had in mind when designing DRA the way it is now.

title: Creation fails when the CRD property is ServiceAccount
body:
### What happened?

My CRD property use the ServiceAccount type, When I use `kubelet apply -f <crds>` to create CRDs generated by controller-gen, get an error message: 
```text
Required value: this property is in x-kubernetes-list-map-keys, so it must have a default or be a required property.
```

This is because ServiceAccount.Secret.Name property is in x-kubernetes-list-map-keys, but it is not have a default and not be a required property.

Structure definition:
```go
// +genclient
// +k8s:deepcopy-gen:interfaces=k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/runtime.Object
// +kubebuilder:...
type Foo struct {
    ServiceAccount corev1.ServiceAccount `json:"serviceAccount,omitempty"`
    ....
}
```

### What did you expect to happen?

I expect to generate CRDs that can be created successfully.

Solutions:
- Set ObjectReference.Name to required. I think the name is required in most scenarios.
- Add default value annotations  (`//+default=""` and `//+kubebuilder:default=""`) for ObjectReference.Name.
- Modify the ServiceAccount.Secrets type to []SecretReference and set SecretReference.name to required.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Refer to "What happened"

title: Incorrect error reporting in case of missing cgroup controllers
body:
### What happened?

If the cgroup validation fails due to missing required controllers (e.g. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/122955) the error that surfaces is, 
```bash
Jun 11 20:22:16 ip-10-0-2-54 kubenswrapper[2176]: E0611 20:22:16.903259    2176 kubelet.go:1559] "Failed to start ContainerManager" err="failed to initialize top level QOS containers: root container [kubepods] doesn't exist"
```
This is incorrect. The code at, https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/d593c886b1fd4119204b8e5a5fc012e36f42fd7a/pkg/kubelet/cm/qos_container_manager_linux.go#L85 

calls https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/d593c886b1fd4119204b8e5a5fc012e36f42fd7a/pkg/kubelet/cm/cgroup_manager_linux.go#L239 but ignores the error. 

This could be quite misleading. In case of https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/122955, the kubelet didn't fail to start because of missing `kubepods` cgroup, but rather due to missing `cpuset`. 

The correct reported error should have been, 

```bash
 Jun 11 20:30:33 ip-10-0-2-54 kubenswrapper[2178]: E0611 20:30:33.085077    2178 kubelet.go:1559] "Failed to start ContainerManager" err="failed to initialize top level QOS containers: error validating root container [kubepods] : cgroup [\"kubepods\"] has some missing controllers: cpuset"
 ```

### What did you expect to happen?

Correct error to propagate when cgroup validation fails during kubelet startup. 

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Everytime kubelet fails to start due to cgroup validation. e.g https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/122955

title: bug: kubelet panic & crash if `--config-dir` is used
body:
### What happened?

I created a v1.30.0 k8s cluster with kubeadm and created a  drop-in directory for kubelet configuration under `/etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf.d`. The normal conf file created by kubeadm is in ` /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml`

According to the [docs](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/administer-cluster/kubelet-config-file/#kubelet-conf-d) the kubelet should merge all configs in specified order and start. But the kubelet crashes under two setups:

**Setup 1**:

The `/etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf.d/20-kubelet.conf` is completely empty the kubelet crashes with:
```
>kubelet --config-dir /etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf.d --config /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml
E0510 13:47:28.749138    9050 run.go:74] "command failed" err="failed to merge kubelet configs: failed to walk through kubelet dropin directory \"/etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf.d\": failed to load kubelet dropin file, path: /etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf.d/20-kubelet.conf, error: kubelet config file \"/etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf.d/20-kubelet.conf\" was empty"
```
If there is just one space or an newline in that file it crashes with:
```
>kubelet --config-dir /etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf.d --config /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml
E0510 13:49:26.243517    9062 run.go:74] "command failed" err=<
        failed to merge kubelet configs: failed to walk through kubelet dropin directory "/etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf.d": failed to load kubelet dropin file, path: /etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf.d/20-kubelet.conf, error: Object 'Kind' is missing in '
        '
```
Even when the docs say:

> These files may contain partial configurations and might not be valid config files by themselves. Validation is only performed on the final resulting configuration structure stored internally in the kubelet. 

If there is nothing or only whitspaces in  `/etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf.d` the merged config should not be invalid and not every file in `/etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf.d` must contain a `kind` property.

**Setup 2**:
The `/etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf.d/20-kubelet.conf` is the same as the `/var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml` the kubelet panics and crashes with:
```
> kubelet --config-dir /etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf.d --config /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml
panic: non-positive interval for NewTicker

goroutine 1 [running]:
time.NewTicker(0xc00098f7a0?)
        time/tick.go:22 +0xe5
k8s.io/klog/v2/internal/clock.RealClock.NewTicker(...)
        k8s.io/klog/v2@v2.120.1/internal/clock/clock.go:111
k8s.io/klog/v2.(*flushDaemon).run(0xc000229650, 0x0)
        k8s.io/klog/v2@v2.120.1/klog.go:1169 +0x10f
k8s.io/klog/v2.StartFlushDaemon(0x0)
        k8s.io/klog/v2@v2.120.1/klog.go:1220 +0x36
k8s.io/component-base/logs/api/v1.apply(0xc0008c8a38, 0x0, {0x7f1ede53b2f0, 0xc000557130})
        k8s.io/component-base/logs/api/v1/options.go:285 +0x890
k8s.io/component-base/logs/api/v1.validateAndApply(0xc0008c8a38, 0x0, {0x7f1ede53b2f0, 0xc000557130}, 0x4?)
        k8s.io/component-base/logs/api/v1/options.go:132 +0x71
k8s.io/component-base/logs/api/v1.ValidateAndApplyAsField(...)
        k8s.io/component-base/logs/api/v1/options.go:124
k8s.io/kubernetes/cmd/kubelet/app.NewKubeletCommand.func1(0xc0000d8908, {0xc000100060, 0x4, 0x4})
        k8s.io/kubernetes/cmd/kubelet/app/server.go:238 +0x4bc
github.com/spf13/cobra.(*Command).execute(0xc0000d8908, {0xc000100060, 0x4, 0x4})
        github.com/spf13/cobra@v1.7.0/command.go:940 +0x882
```

Using the same config only via `--config` works.

### What did you expect to happen?

The kubelet should start with empty files in `/etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf.d` or if the files in `/var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml` and `/etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf.d` are the same.

The second issue I encountered was that I used the exact same config (with api version and kind) via `--config` and as an drop-in config file and the kubelet crashed with the above error. (See setup 2) Are `--config` and the `--config-dir` meant to be mutually exclusive? Which one takes precedence over the over? Both in terms of flags and config file.

>The second issue I encountered was that I used the exact same config (with api version and kind) via --config and as an drop-in config file and the kubelet crashed with the above error. (See setup 2) Are --config and the --config-dir meant to be mutually exclusive? Which one takes precedence over the over? Both in terms of flags and config file.

These two options are not mutually exclusive; they are designed to work together. When both are used, the kubelet should first load the configuration from the `--config` file and then apply any settings from the files in the `--config-dir`, with the latter taking precedence. This means that if there are conflicting settings, those in the drop-in directory will override those specified in the primary configuration file. Regarding the issue, the kubelet should be able to handle such scenarios gracefully without resulting in a crash. I will work on it once the enhancement freeze is over.

title: Custom resource objects can be created during CRD Termination using server-side apply
body:
### What happened?

After a CRD DELETE, while the CRD finalizer is deleting all custom resource objects of that type, and the `Terminating=True` status condition is set, it should not be possible to create objects of that type, but it is with server-side apply, because the creation prevention implementation blocks by method type and there's no check in the PATCH handler.

- CREATE is blocked: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/apiserver/customresource_handler.go#L373
- PATCH is not blocked: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/apiserver/customresource_handler.go#L390

In the Patch Apply handler, the `forceAllowCreate` flag is set to `true`: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers/patch.go#L646 This allows patching to always create objects.

### What did you expect to happen?

When the CRD is terminating, SSA should not be able to create new objects.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. apply a CRD
2. apply a CR with a manual finalizer to block CRD termination
3. delete the CRD
4. create a new CR with SSA

### Anything else we need to know?

There is another race condition allowing creation, but it's otherwise unrelated to this bug, which is not a race condition: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/99181

```console
$ kubectl version
Client Version: v1.28.2
Kustomize Version: v5.0.4-0.20230601165947-6ce0bf390ce3
Server Version: v1.27.4-gke.900
```

</details>

title: NoExecute taint is added with extra 5s delay when a Node's ready condition becomes Unknown
body:
### What happened?

When investigating a delay of Pod eviction on unreachable Node, I found it always took 5s longer than the desired duration.
Looking at the timestamps, I found an odd one: the timestamp when `node.kubernetes.io/unreachable` NoExecute taint was added.

```
# Node taints:
taints:
- effect: NoSchedule
  key: node.kubernetes.io/unreachable
  timeAdded: "2023-09-21T06:32:41Z"
- effect: NoExecute
  key: node.kubernetes.io/unreachable
  timeAdded: "2023-09-21T06:32:46Z"    # This one is 5s later than all other timestamps

# Node conditions:
conditions:
- lastHeartbeatTime: "2023-09-21T06:31:55Z"
  lastTransitionTime: "2023-09-21T06:32:41Z"
  message: Kubelet stopped posting node status.
  reason: NodeStatusUnknown
  status: Unknown
  type: MemoryPressure
- lastHeartbeatTime: "2023-09-21T06:31:55Z"
  lastTransitionTime: "2023-09-21T06:32:41Z"
  message: Kubelet stopped posting node status.
  reason: NodeStatusUnknown
  status: Unknown
  type: DiskPressure
- lastHeartbeatTime: "2023-09-21T06:31:55Z"
  lastTransitionTime: "2023-09-21T06:32:41Z"
  message: Kubelet stopped posting node status.
  reason: NodeStatusUnknown
  status: Unknown
  type: PIDPressure
- lastHeartbeatTime: "2023-09-21T06:31:55Z"
  lastTransitionTime: "2023-09-21T06:32:41Z"
  message: Kubelet stopped posting node status.
  reason: NodeStatusUnknown
  status: Unknown
  type: Ready

# Pod conditions:
- lastProbeTime: null
  lastTransitionTime: "2023-09-21T06:32:41Z"
  status: "False"
  type: Ready
```

This can be reproducd consistently by terminating kubelet on a Node. The 5s delay of tainting adds 5s delay to the recovery time of Pods which are supposed to be evicted by the taint and recreated on other Nodes sooner. And I can't think of a reason why this taint alone should be added 5s later after the other taint and all other status changes. After investigating the relevant code for how the 5s is introduced, I think it should be an unwanted effect:

`processTaintBaseEviction()` uses the last observed ready condition of the Node instead of the current one to determine whether it should add the Node to the taint queue. When a Node is set to unreachable due to missing heartbeats, the last observed ready condition is still `true` and the current ready condition is `unknown`, we should use the latter for `processTaintBaseEviction()`. Otherwise the taint can only be added when `monitorNodeHealth()` runs another time (5s later) during which the current ready condition becomes the last observed ready condition, like the following logs show:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/cde6a46a483a0cc7d3f2404db506e1c24ecd4e9d/pkg/controller/nodelifecycle/node_lifecycle_controller.go#L741

```

I0921 13:38:27.930777       1 node_lifecycle_controller.go:954] "Node hasn't been updated" node="kind-worker2" duration="40.006732434s" nodeConditionType=MemoryPressure currentCondition="&NodeCondition{Type:MemoryPressure,Status:False,LastHeartbeatTime:2023-09-21 13:35:27 +0000 UTC,LastTransitionTime:2023-09-21 13:35:27 +0000 UTC,Reason:KubeletHasSufficientMemory,Message:kubelet has sufficient memory available,}"
I0921 13:38:27.930881       1 node_lifecycle_controller.go:954] "Node hasn't been updated" node="kind-worker2" duration="40.006958941s" nodeConditionType=DiskPressure currentCondition="&NodeCondition{Type:DiskPressure,Status:False,LastHeartbeatTime:2023-09-21 13:35:27 +0000 UTC,LastTransitionTime:2023-09-21 13:35:27 +0000 UTC,Reason:KubeletHasNoDiskPressure,Message:kubelet has no disk pressure,}"
I0921 13:38:27.930931       1 node_lifecycle_controller.go:954] "Node hasn't been updated" node="kind-worker2" duration="40.007072433s" nodeConditionType=PIDPressure currentCondition="&NodeCondition{Type:PIDPressure,Status:False,LastHeartbeatTime:2023-09-21 13:35:27 +0000 UTC,LastTransitionTime:2023-09-21 13:35:27 +0000 UTC,Reason:KubeletHasSufficientPID,Message:kubelet has sufficient PID available,}"
I0921 13:38:27.940640       1 controller_utils.go:186] "Recording status change event message for node" status="NodeNotReady" node="kind-worker2"
I0921 13:38:27.940700       1 controller_utils.go:123] "Update ready status of pods on node" node="kind-worker2"
I0921 13:38:27.940803       1 controller_utils.go:144] "Updating ready status of pod to false" pod="kube-system/antrea-agent-sw57p"
I0921 13:38:27.941226       1 event.go:307] "Event occurred" object="kind-worker2" fieldPath="" kind="Node" apiVersion="v1" type="Normal" reason="NodeNotReady" message="Node kind-worker2 status is now: NodeNotReady"
I0921 13:38:27.952517       1 controller_utils.go:144] "Updating ready status of pod to false" pod="kube-system/kube-proxy-ktsph"
I0921 13:38:27.952879       1 event.go:307] "Event occurred" object="kube-system/antrea-agent-sw57p" fieldPath="" kind="Pod" apiVersion="v1" type="Warning" reason="NodeNotReady" message="Node is not ready"
I0921 13:38:27.961405       1 event.go:307] "Event occurred" object="kube-system/kube-proxy-ktsph" fieldPath="" kind="Pod" apiVersion="v1" type="Warning" reason="NodeNotReady" message="Node is not ready"
# Second round handling after the Node is detected as unreachable.
I0921 13:38:32.962342       1 node_lifecycle_controller.go:954] "Node hasn't been updated" node="kind-worker2" duration="45.038461632s" nodeConditionType=Ready currentCondition="&NodeCondition{Type:Ready,Status:Unknown,LastHeartbeatTime:2023-09-21 13:35:27 +0000 UTC,LastTransitionTime:2023-09-21 13:38:27 +0000 UTC,Reason:NodeStatusUnknown,Message:Kubelet stopped posting node status.,}"
I0921 13:38:32.962379       1 node_lifecycle_controller.go:954] "Node hasn't been updated" node="kind-worker2" duration="45.038523697s" nodeConditionType=MemoryPressure currentCondition="&NodeCondition{Type:MemoryPressure,Status:Unknown,LastHeartbeatTime:2023-09-21 13:35:27 +0000 UTC,LastTransitionTime:2023-09-21 13:38:27 +0000 UTC,Reason:NodeStatusUnknown,Message:Kubelet stopped posting node status.,}"
I0921 13:38:32.962408       1 node_lifecycle_controller.go:954] "Node hasn't been updated" node="kind-worker2" duration="45.038548769s" nodeConditionType=DiskPressure currentCondition="&NodeCondition{Type:DiskPressure,Status:Unknown,LastHeartbeatTime:2023-09-21 13:35:27 +0000 UTC,LastTransitionTime:2023-09-21 13:38:27 +0000 UTC,Reason:NodeStatusUnknown,Message:Kubelet stopped posting node status.,}"
I0921 13:38:32.962431       1 node_lifecycle_controller.go:954] "Node hasn't been updated" node="kind-worker2" duration="45.03857838s" nodeConditionType=PIDPressure currentCondition="&NodeCondition{Type:PIDPressure,Status:Unknown,LastHeartbeatTime:2023-09-21 13:35:27 +0000 UTC,LastTransitionTime:2023-09-21 13:38:27 +0000 UTC,Reason:NodeStatusUnknown,Message:Kubelet stopped posting node status.,}"
# The node is added to the taint queue only in the second round.
I0921 13:38:32.962509       1 node_lifecycle_controller.go:793] "Node is unresponsive. Adding it to the Taint queue" node="kind-worker2" timeStamp="2023-09-21 13:38:32.962484274 +0000 UTC m=+71.367258065"
```

I will create a PR to fix it if the above analysis makes sense.

### What did you expect to happen?

`node.kubernetes.io/unreachable` NoExecute taint shouldn't be added with extra 5s delay, compared with when `node.kubernetes.io/unreachable` NoSchedule taint is added and the Node is detected as unhealthy.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Stop kubelet on one Node.
2. Check the timestamps of the taints and condition transition of the Node.

#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

After a Node has stopped posting heartbeats for nodeMonitorGracePeriod, it will be considered unreachable, its ready condition will be set to Unknown, NoSchedule taint will be added, all Pods on it will be set to NotReady, but there is always a delay of 5s before NoExecute taint is added to the Node, adding 5s to the recovery time of Pods which are supposed to be evicted by the taint and recreated on other Nodes sooner.

The delay is because processTaintBaseEviction() uses the last observed ready condition of the Node instead of the current one to determine whether it should add the Node to the taint queue. When a Node is set to unreachable due to missing heartbeats, the last observed ready condition is still true and the current ready condition is unknown, we should use the latter for processTaintBaseEviction().

### What happened?

target file: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/util/workqueue/queue_test.go
```

1. for _, test := range tests {
2. 	const producers = 50
3. 	producerWG := sync.WaitGroup{}
4. 	producerWG.Add(producers)
5. 	for i := 0; i < producers; i++ {
6. 		go func(i int) {
7. 			defer producerWG.Done()
8. 			for j := 0; j < 50; j++ {
9. 				test.queue.Add(i)
10. 				time.Sleep(time.Millisecond)
11. 			}
12. 		}(i)
13. 	}
14. 
15. 	// Start consumers
16. 	const consumers = 10
17. 	consumerWG := sync.WaitGroup{}
18. 	consumerWG.Add(consumers)
19. 	for i := 0; i < consumers; i++ {
20. 		go func(i int) {
21. 			defer consumerWG.Done()
22. 			for {
23. 				item, quit := test.queue.Get()
24. 				if item == "added after shutdown!" {
25. 					t.Errorf("Got an item added after shutdown.")
26. 				}
27. 				if quit {
28. 					return
29. 				}
30. 				t.Logf("Worker %v: begin processing %v", i, item)
31. 				time.Sleep(3 * time.Millisecond)
32. 				t.Logf("Worker %v: done processing %v", i, item)
33. 				test.queue.Done(item)
34. 			}
35. 		}(i)
36. 	}
37. 
38. 	producerWG.Wait()
39. }
```

**In the func TestBasic(), the loop variable `test` is captured by 'func' literals in 'go' statements (at Line9 and Line33), it may cause a data race. title: Deployment names can be too long, such that ReplicaSet creation fails

nodes.body: hey @thockin I'm new to k8s ,but i want to try fix this issue. If the deployment name with the replicaset suffix is longer than 253 characters, or the deployment name with the pod suffix is longer than 253 characters, truncate the deployment name and trigger a warning. Do you think logic is right?

I think there are a couple ways this could be approached, which need some consideration.  Off the top of my head:

1) Require that Deployment's name be less than 242 (253 - 10 for hash - 1 for '-') characters.  This seems like a breaking change, but no deployment with that name could ever actually WORK, so acceptable.

2) Accept long names but internally truncate to 242 when creating the replicaset(s).  This leaves room for the replicaset suffix, but that will again be truncated when the pod is created with `generateName`, which only uses 63 characters.  This already generates a warning, so maybe OK?  This will break anyone who tries to parse the RS name and extract the deployment name.

3) Accept long names but internally truncate to fit `generateName` (e.g. 46 (63 - 10 for hash - 1 for '-' - 6 for pod random suffix) when creating the replicaset(s). This will break anyone who tries to parse the RS name and extract the deployment name.

4) Just issue a warning when the name will result in failure (I dislike this option).

No matter what you do, there's a potential for clients who depend on undefined behavior.  For example, they parse out the last `-.{5}` of the pod name to get the replicaset name, and the last `-.{10}` to get the deployment name.  For very long names they will be broken, but they kind of are broken already.

There are almost certainly other options that make different/better tradeoffs, too!

This seems like the best solution to me as we would not break any working deployments.

Even though the recommended approach for matching the Deployments and ReplicaSets is OwnerReferences or Labels, we cannot be sure that people are not using the quick and dirty approach of checking for just the name only (e.g. in scripts, tests).

>> 1. Require that Deployment's name be less than 242 (253 - 10 for hash - 1 for '-') characters.
>
> This seems like the best solution to me as we would not break any working deployments.

This is the least impactful change, but I think it's still less than ideal.  Just to be really clear, even ignoring the outright failure mode I reported initially, it is bad in other cases:

What happens today with a long name:
* Create deployment `<59 chars name>`
* Creates RS `<59 chars name>-<10 char hash>`
* Creates pods `<58 chars (truncated)><5 char random>` - note, the hash is totally gone

It's impossible to parse that into either Deployment name or ReplicaSet name.  Both have been obscured.  Worse, if you happen to have 2 long-name Deployments which are the same initial 58 characters, the pods are indistinguishable by name.

But also:
* Create deployment `<48 chars name>`
* Creates RS `<48 chars name>-<10 char hash>`
* Creates pods `<48 chars name>-<9 char hash (truncated)><5 char random>`

At 48 characters, the deployment name survives, but the hash is obscured, so RS name is lost.

This is why I sort of lean to option 3, personally - the pod name includes the whole RS name, but the RS name is a truncated form of the deployment.  I think that's a better tradeoff because humans look at pod names more than RS names, and grouping matters, so optimizing for the better pod names is better.  But I can sort of buy the argument for option 1 too.

> What happens today with a long name:
>    Creates pods <58 chars (truncated)><5 char random> - note, the hash is totally gone

Do users care more about persisting Deployment - RS pairing, or RS - Pod pairing? I agree, it would look better to persist RS - Pod pairing.

Nevertheless this would only get fixed for deployments. Anyone creating replicas manually or by other means, will break the consistency. So you cannot be sure that you can always pair the Pod back to RS, which reduces the benefit a bit. Which you can do with Deployment - RS pairing now, except for the extremely long case.

Certainly needs to be discussed in a SIG meeting. If people think the risk of breaking someone is low, we can do option 3.  We could also do option 1 and 3 at the same time to trim the allowed names a bit.

> Nevertheless this would only get fixed for deployments. Anyone creating replicas manually or by other means, will break the consistency. So you cannot be sure that you can always pair the Pod back to RS

This is true - we can only fix the parts we control, and we don't have a general "append to the name" model because it's complex to design something really useful and because parsing the name is (in general) an anti-pattern.  We know that a pod could be orphaned from an RS/Deployment and adopted by another.  At that point, the pod's name is a staight-up LIE.  :)

It's unfortunate that Deployment becomes aware of RelicaSet's implementation details (i.e. if RS didn't use `generateName`, we'd be having a different discussion!).  Ideally, Deployment would just make totally random RS names, and RS would make totally random pod names, and nobody would parse them - not in code and not visually.  But that's a crappy human UX for the most common path.

> I think there are a couple ways this could be approached, which need some consideration. Off the top of my head:

This leaves room for the replicaset suffix, but that will again be truncated when the pod is created with `generateName`, which only uses 63 characters. > 3. Accept long names but internally truncate to fit `generateName` (e.g. 46 (63 - 10 for hash - 1 for '-' - 6 for pod random suffix) when creating the replicaset(s). This will break anyone who tries to parse the RS name and extract the deployment name.
> 4. Just issue a warning when the name will result in failure (I dislike this option).

@thockin Sig apps think option 1 would be better.

So if we pursued option 1, Deployments would have shorter names, ReplicaSets would have long names, and Pods would have gibberish names.  https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/116447#issuecomment-1496210300

Is that really well understood?  I am a little surprised, personally, but OK.

Should we take this as an opportunity to update docs to express that the name-relationship between Deployment -> RS -> Pod is NOT part of the API contract, and should not be depended on?

> Why does generateName limit to only 63 characters, if Pod name limit is
> 253?
>
> To recap on ability to parse: users can parse a Deployment name from any
> Replicaset name, but they cannot parse either Deployment or Replicaset
> names from a Pod name, reliably.
>
> To break or not to break 🤔
>
> See #64023 (comment)
> <https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/64023#issuecomment-1531459619>
> for a related discussion, where we decided not to change validation.
>
> —
> Reply to this email directly, view it on GitHub
> <https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/116447#issuecomment-1531460764>,
> or unsubscribe
> <https://github.com/notifications/unsubscribe-auth/ABKWAVFIQBJLDFCCDK2Q35DXEECQPANCNFSM6AAAAAAVVYJJBE>
> .
> You are receiving this because you were mentioned.Message ID:
> ***@***.***>
>

I see. So there is no world where we can make Pod from ReplicaSets have longer names. And that limits the length of the name of a Deployment significantly.

If we are ok with breaking users that might be parsing a Deployment name from a ReplicaSet name, then I'm ok with solution 3. I wouldn't expect there to be many, as opposed to ones trying to parse a Deployment name from Pod, which is already broken.

What do we gain? The ability to create working Deployments with slightly longer names, which might be useful.

> So there is no world where we can make Pod from ReplicaSets have longer
names

Well, RS doesn't *have to* use generateName, it's just convenient.  It
could generate names itself (as does deployment).  But any pod name > 63
will be weird for hostname, so we recommend not to do that (API warning).

I wish we had just kept it simple all along. :)

> If we are ok with breaking users that might be parsing a Deployment name
from a ReplicaSet name, then I'm ok with solution 3. I wouldn't expect
there to be many, as opposed to ones trying to parse a Deployment name from
Pod, which is already broken

Keep in mind that for "reasonable" names (less than 40ish) this is all
fine.  It's only beyond that that matters.

What I liked about 3 is that it optimizes for humans looking at 'get pods'.
But I am not trying to override the SIG, just make sure the options are
clear.

The [Deployment doc ](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/controllers/deployment/) said:
> Notice that the name of the ReplicaSet is always formatted as [DEPLOYMENT-NAME]-[HASH]. This name will become the basis for the Pods which are created.

I'm not sure how many users rely on it. Given that we documented it, there might be some. 

Also thanks Tim for the detailed explanation. I like that option 3 not only solves the name length issue (which I think doesn't worth breaking RS name), but also fix the UX issue with name awkwardness. 

Deployment has hash collision avoidance mechanism for RS name hash, so shortening it wouldn't cause problems with name collision.

Another option could be for RS not to use generateName directly but instead
generate its own pod names of the form <46 chars deployment name>-<10 chars
hash>-<5 random>.

To do that, it would have to have the deployment name and hash as distinct
values (or else we end up parsing the name!).  This only works for
Deployment - if someone else uses RS directly we wouldn't know to do this,
unless we formalize something more. Maybe using the owner ref?

On Tue, May 2, 2023, 7:05 PM Janet Kuo ***@***.***> wrote:

> The Deployment doc
> <https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/controllers/deployment/>
> said:
>
> Notice that the name of the ReplicaSet is always formatted as
> [DEPLOYMENT-NAME]-[HASH]. This name will become the basis for the Pods
> which are created.
>
> I'm not sure how many users rely on it. Given that we documented it there
> might be some.
>
> Also thanks Tim for the detailed explanation. I like that option 3 not
> only solves the name length issue (which I think doesn't worth breaking RS
> name), but also fix the UX issue with name awkwardness.
>
> Deployment has hash collision mechanism for RS name hash, so shortening it
> wouldn't cause problems with name collision.
>
> —
> Reply to this email directly, view it on GitHub
> <https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/116447#issuecomment-1532370958>,
> or unsubscribe
> <https://github.com/notifications/unsubscribe-auth/ABKWAVB6RT6YFKQLOP6NIPTXEG4PZANCNFSM6AAAAAAVVYJJBE>
> .
> You are receiving this because you were mentioned.Message ID:
> ***@***.***>
>
How should we do next?

@janetkuo @kow3ns your call.

I feel the details have been laid out.

Option 1) `rs.name = trunc(deployment.name, 242) + hash; pod.name = truncate(rs.name, 58) + random` -- optimize for fidelity in deployment->rs names at the cost of pod names

Option 3) `rs.name = truncate(deployment.name, 46) + hash; pod.name = rs.name + random` -- optimize for human-friendlier pod names at the cost of rs names

Option X) change how RS generates pod names completely

This issue has been blocking for a long time and @janetkuo @kow3ns have not responded.
@thockin How can we move forward and solve this issue?
re https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/116447#issuecomment-1548246577 I slightly prefer 1 that optimizes for fidelity in deployment->rs names. @kow3ns WDYT?
@hysyeah are you still planning to work on this?

### What happened?

When a larger value is passed to the `resourceVersion` parameter and the` limit` parameter is set to a larger value, the response will return 500error with the message "etcdserver: mvcc: required revision is a future revision".
## Q2: Delete Request error
When constructing a delete request with one or more error parameters, I get a 500 response code and the same error message "converting (v1.APIResourceList) to (v1.DeleteOptions): unknown conversion", which makes it unclear to me which parameter is the error
I found this error in multiple endpoints(my guess is that any operation involving delete will trigger this kind of problem):
`/apis/batch/v1/namespaces/{namespace}/cronjobs`
`/api/v1/persistentvolumes/{name}`
`/apis/node.k8s.io/v1/runtimeclasses`
## Q3: Json parse error
When a parameter in the request references the API spec "#/definitions/io.k8s.apimachinery.pkg.apis.meta.v1.DeleteOptions" and is passed a parameter type that is different from the template definition. then you will receive 500 code with message "couldn\\'t get version/kind; json parse error: json: cannot unmarshal xxxinto Go struct field xxx of type xxx"

title: Admission webhooks don't match changes on subresources like Scale
body:
### What happened?

I have a statefulset with a label `colega.eu/webhook`:

`workload.yaml`:
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: workload
  labels:
    colega.eu/webhook: 'true'
spec:
  replicas: 1
  serviceName: workload
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: workload
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: workload
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nothing
        image: alpine
        command: ["/bin/watch"]
        args: ["-t", "-n", "2", "date"]
```

And I've created a webhook for changes in `statefulsets` and `statefulsets/scale` that have that the `colega.eu/webhook=true` label:

```yaml
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1
kind: ValidatingWebhookConfiguration
metadata:
  name: webhook
webhooks:
- name: webhook.colega.eu
  clientConfig:
    service:
      name: something-that-does-not-exist
      namespace: default
      path: /webhook
      port: 443
  objectSelector:
    matchLabels:
      colega.eu/webhook: 'true'
  rules:
  - apiGroups: ["apps"]
    apiVersions: ["v1"]
    operations: ["UPDATE"]
    resources: ["statefulsets"]
    scope: Namespaced
  - apiGroups: ["apps"]
    apiVersions: ["v1"]
    operations: ["*"]
    resources: ["statefulsets/scale"]
    scope: '*'
  admissionReviewVersions:
  - v1
  sideEffects: None
  failurePolicy: Fail
```

When I try to update my statefulset, the webhook is called (and it fails as the webhook service doesn't exist):
```
$ kubectl patch statefulsets.apps workload --patch='{"spec": {"replicas": 2}}'
Error from server (InternalError): Internal error occurred: failed calling webhook "webhook.colega.eu": Post "https://something-that-does-not-exist.default.svc:443/webhook?timeout=10s": service "something-that-does-not-exist" not found
```

However, when I update it using `kubectl scale` subcommand it does not call the webhook:
```
$ kubectl scale statefulset workload --replicas 2                             
statefulset.apps/workload scaled
```

However, the statefulset's `spec.replicas` field is updated.

### What did you expect to happen?

I expected the `kubectl scale` command to also fail, as I'd expect the `statefulset/scale` subresource to have the same labels as the parent resource (because the subresource doesn't have labels). 

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

<details>

<summary>Click me to expand</summary>

```
$ cat workload.yaml 
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: workload
  labels:
    colega.eu/webhook: 'true'
spec:
  replicas: 1
  serviceName: workload
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: workload
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: workload
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nothing
        image: alpine
        command: ["/bin/watch"]
        args: ["-t", "-n", "2", "date"]

$ cat webhook.yaml 
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1
kind: ValidatingWebhookConfiguration
metadata:
  name: webhook
webhooks:
- name: webhook.colega.eu
  clientConfig:
    service:
      name: something-that-does-not-exist
      namespace: default
      path: /webhook
      port: 443
  objectSelector:
    matchLabels:
      colega.eu/webhook: 'true'
  rules:
  - apiGroups: ["apps"]
    apiVersions: ["v1"]
    operations: ["UPDATE"]
    resources: ["statefulsets"]
    scope: Namespaced
  - apiGroups: ["apps"]
    apiVersions: ["v1"]
    operations: ["*"]
    resources: ["statefulsets/scale"]
    scope: '*'
  admissionReviewVersions:
  - v1
  sideEffects: None
  failurePolicy: Fail

$ kubectl apply -f workload.yaml 
statefulset.apps/workload created

$ kubectl apply -f webhook.yaml 
validatingwebhookconfiguration.admissionregistration.k8s.io/webhook created

$ kubectl patch statefulsets.apps workload --patch='{"spec": {"replicas": 2}}'
Error from server (InternalError): Internal error occurred: failed calling webhook "webhook.colega.eu": Post "https://something-that-does-not-exist.default.svc:443/webhook?timeout=10s": service "something-that-does-not-exist" not found

$ kubectl scale statefulset workload --replicas 2
statefulset.apps/workload scaled
```
</details>

### Anything else we need to know?

I know that [the documentation states](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/extensible-admission-controllers/#matching-requests-objectselector) that:

> Use the object selector only if the webhook is opt-in, because end users may skip the admission webhook by setting the labels.

However, I'm not trying to prevent users from skipping the webhook here, I'm trying to catch changes to legitimately opted-in statefulsets replicas.

I can't see any way of creating a webhook without removing the label matchers on it (which would be highly undesired as there are a lot of objects that I don't want to validate in our clusters) and manually (from the webhook) accessing the deployment through the API when the validating request arrives to check whether it contains or not the labels.



### Kubernetes version

```console
$ kubectl version  
Client Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"22", GitVersion:"v1.22.3", GitCommit:"c92036820499fedefec0f847e2054d824aea6cd1", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2021-10-27T18:41:28Z", GoVersion:"go1.16.9", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"linux/amd64"}
```

Use `apiGroups: ["autoscaling"]` for the scale subresource? Also note is has both a v1 and v2 API (but matchType=Equivalent, which is the default, should be enough to match)

I just tried with this rule:
```
  - apiGroups: ["autoscaling"]
    apiVersions: ["v1"]

```

And even with no `objectSelectors`, the webhook isn't being called when `kubectl scale` operation is applied. (I even tried with `*` as apiVersions, with no luck).

I can see that `autoscaling/v1/Scale` does have the ObjectMeta in it, and it would be great to see it being checked in the scale operation.

Thank you for the quick response, but that didn't work neither.

Tried this locally and I understand what is going on.

Apologies for my earlier suggestions. There were going in the wrong direction.

Changes to the autoscaling subresources are matched based on the apiGroup and apiVersion of the resource.  For example:

```
       - apiGroups:   ["apps"]                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
         apiVersions: ["*"]                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             
         operations:  ["CREATE", "UPDATE"]                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
         resources:   ["*/scale"]   
```

Matches the subresource of a deployment, which can be validated  by using:

```
kubectl scale deploy/nginx-deployment --replicas=2
```

The problem with the original example in this issue is that the request to change scale was made to the statefulset resource directly, and not to the scale subresource of the statefulset.

A webhook that intends to intercept all changes to scale would need to match both the root resource and the scale subresource in a case like this, and handle both, since the scale fields exist in both resources.

```yaml
    operations: ["CREATE", "UPDATE"]
    resources: ["*/scale"]
    scope: Namespaced

  - v1

```

And then
```
$ kubectl scale statefulset workload --replicas 3

```

Which succeeds (but it shouldn't, as it should call the non-existent webhook).

> The problem with the original example in this issue is that the request to change scale was made to the statefulset resource directly, and not to the scale subresource of the statefulset.

I didn't understand this. I always tried with `kubectl scale statefulset ...`, doesn't that modify the scale subresource?

In order to ensure we're on the same page, just to be clear: the _problem_ for me is that the request _succeeds_, as it shouln't because the webhook endpoint doesn't exist.

This does bring up some interesting questions of how matching should work to support this use case better.

edit: @colega Would you be willing to open a separate issue that describes the need to match a scale subresource only for root objects with specific labels set? Off the top of my head I can't think of how to do that with the existing matching system.

It might not play nicely with the original write-contention-avoidance goal, but would help avoid the need for users to write policies against multiple different shapes of requests to prevent, say, over-scaling requests at request time.

title: Inconceivable: dispatch before arrival - apparent APF error
body:
### What happened?

Running a load test on K8s 1.23.5, and I got some messages like this:

```
\"Inconceivable!\" err=\"dispatch before arrival\" QS=\"system\" queue=0 dispatchR=\"6570.26436833ss\" request=... flowDistinguisher:system:node:[redacted] fsName:system-nodes ... workEstimate:{WorkEstimate:{InitialSeats:1 FinalSeats:0 AdditionalLatency:0} totalWork:300000 finalWork:0} ... arrivalTime:{wall:13887921938884605587 ext:18745363038248 ... arrivalR:657026745599 startTime:{wall:0 ext:0 loc:<nil>} waitStarted:false}
```

### What did you expect to happen?

It runs without inconceivable errors

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

I don't have a good repro, sorry.  Output is from an internal load test that we run here at AKS. There were other errors logged around the same time (so maybe there's some load-related issue in the cluster that caused the problem - I haven't checked that at this time).  Just figured I'd better log this issue because, given the wording of the error message, I figured someone might like to know.  

### Kubernetes version

1.23.5


### Cloud provider

AKS

nodes.body: /sig api-machinery
cc @MikeSpreitzer
/triage accepted
@JohnRusk : are there any "queue::nextDispatchR underflow" or "request::arrivalR underflow" messages logged from the same (or any other) apiserver?
What do the `apiserver_flowcontrol_epoch_advance_total` metrics say?
Any "queueset::currentR overflow" log messages?

What was the `-v` setting?
I assume it was less than 4, and no "AntiWindup tweaked queue" messages appeared.

Can you retry, with verbosity targeted specifically at https://github.com/kubernetes/apiserver/blob/v0.23.5/pkg/util/flowcontrol/fairqueuing/queueset/queueset.go#L948 ?

That, and the metric, would help confirm or deny two hypotheses about what's going wrong.
Let me see what I can do.  (The test in question was run by another team, so it will take me a little while to talk it over with them etc).

I found a path through the code that should not be there.  I do not know whether it is the cause of what @JohnRusk is reporting here.  It is a path that avoids the simple direct enforcement in queueSet::boundNextDispatchLocked (https://github.com/kubernetes/apiserver/blob/v0.23.5/pkg/util/flowcontrol/fairqueuing/queueset/queueset.go#L941).  It goes as follows.

- https://github.com/kubernetes/apiserver/blob/v0.23.5/pkg/util/flowcontrol/fairqueuing/queueset/queueset.go#L396 (in request::wait) removes a request from the queue, possibly the oldest one, after which the queue's oldest request will have a higher arrivalR and that could be higher than the queue's nextDispatchR.
- https://github.com/kubernetes/apiserver/blob/v0.23.5/pkg/util/flowcontrol/fairqueuing/queueset/queueset.go#L348 , in request::Finish, calls request::wait and in this case will return without calling queueSet::boundNextDispatchLocked.

I've been in touch with the team that ran the test, and had a look at their logs. Unfortunately, the problem doesn't normally happen. I.e. in most test runs, the error doesn't happen.  This means that we can't reproduce the issue at will, so I don't currently have a good way of doing the verbosity change and metrics gathering. (Since those are not automated, and would have to be done manually).  If I think of a way, I'll post here.

Meanwhile, glad to hear that one plausible cause has been found.

### What happened?

```go
ns := os.Getenv("ns")
```

My namespace is obtained from the environment variable. When I don't set it, the code can return all clusterrole, but when I set the `ns`  environment variable, it will report an error `the server could not find the requested resource`

title: Kubelet should enforce that static pods do not reference other API objects
body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


#### What happened:
I put into `/etc/kubernetes/manifests/` one defining a static pod with a `serviceAccount`, because I was wondering if this is supported (the documentation does not say, see https://github.com/kubernetes/website/issues/28611#issuecomment-876537379).  The kubelet created the pod but without giving it the relevant mount.  The kubelet did _not_ create the corresponding mirror pod.

Here is the manifest I created:
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: test5
spec:
  containers:
  - name: bb
    image: busybox
    command:
    - sleep
    - "864001"
  serviceAccountName: default
```
Here are some relevant log entries from the kubelet:
```
Jul 08 15:55:05 init1 kubelet[4229]: I0708 15:55:05.335792    4229 kubelet.go:1681] "Creating a mirror pod for static pod" pod="default/test5-init1"

Jul 08 15:55:05 init1 kubelet[4229]: E0708 15:55:05.343771    4229 kubelet.go:1683] "Failed creating a mirror pod for" err="pods \"test5-init1\" is forbidden: a mirror pod may not reference service accounts" pod="default/test5-init1"
```

#### What you expected to happen:
I expected consistent treatment --- real pod and mirror pod both exist or both do not exist.

#### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):
I think the above is pretty minimal.

#### Anything else we need to know?:

#### Environment:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`):
  ```
  Client Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"21", GitVersion:"v1.21.1", GitCommit:"5e58841cce77d4bc13713ad2b91fa0d961e69192", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2021-05-12T14:18:45Z", GoVersion:"go1.16.4", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"linux/amd64"}

  ```

- Install tools: kubeadm v1.21.2

nodes.body: @kubernetes/sig-node-bugs

It is expected that static pod will not run... no references to API objects are permitted in static pods (service accounts, PVC objects, secrets, configmaps, etc). 

> The kubelet created the pod but without giving it the relevant mount. The kubelet did not create the corresponding mirror pod.

I'm not sure I understand what you mean by this

Ooh, the prohibition is even broader.  @liggitt please have a look at https://github.com/kubernetes/website/pull/28623 and there should probably also be updates to PodSpec and/or types inside it.

Adding SIG storage since volume mounts outside of host path and empty dir do not make sense for static pods.
xref: https://github.com/kubernetes/website/pull/28623 https://github.com/kubernetes/website/issues/28611 #103167

the HEAD commit at https://github.com/liggitt/kubernetes/commits/kubelet-static-api-reference is a sketch of what this could look like, catching API references in file and url sourced pods and preventing them from ever being handled by the kubelet

/assign

Agreed this should be blocked at creation time
Is this enforced at API today?  Is there any backward compatibility implication to tightening Kubelet validation?

> Is this enforced at API today?

Yes, NodeRestriction admission blocks the serviceaccount/secret/configmap/pvc references that would inform node authorizer:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/0270fc75d0f59e1f5a31a810737ac35ac3eeb8a3/plugin/pkg/admission/noderestriction/admission.go#L247-L265

Blocking pod creation there means the node is silently running static pods that *probably* aren't working (API references that require authz fail unless another pod on the same node happens to reference the same API object), and *definitely* are confusing the scheduler because the resources they consume aren't represented in the API.

> Is there any backward compatibility implication to tightening Kubelet validation?

A kubelet could conceivably be running static pods whose referenced resources *happened* to also be referenced by a non-static pod on the same node, but that doesn't seem like it would result in consistently successful pods.
xref https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/113374 which is adding another API reference field to protect against in static / mirror pods

#### What type of PR is this?

/kind feature

<!--
Add one of the following kinds:
/kind bug

/kind documentation
/kind feature

Optionally add one or more of the following kinds if applicable:
/kind api-change
/kind deprecation
/kind failing-test
/kind flake
/kind regression
-->

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Currently, mirror pod reconciliation for static pods which reference API objects will fail. However the pod itself is not denied admission and the node would be silently running the static pod's container. As discussed in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/103587#issuecomment-2433035095, we want to tighten the validation here so that pod would not be running at all in the node. Currently the static pod would be running in the node while the mirror pod would not be created (which is enforced in the API as per https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/103587#issuecomment-1456581669). This PR updates the validation logic so that the pod is denied admission for static pods referencing API objects and make sure that the container is not created in the node.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
<!--
*Automatically closes linked issue when PR is merged.
Usage: `Fixes #<issue number>`, or `Fixes (paste link of issue)`.
_If PR is about `failing-tests or flakes`, please post the related issues/tests in a comment and do not use `Fixes`_*
-->
Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/103587

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

Notes:
- I've added a new StaticPodAdmitHandler so that this validation is done from `canAdmitPod`. This is based on @gjkim42's comment https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/105368#issuecomment-984576615.
- The structure of the handler and the tests were inspired from the `PredicateAdmitHandler` in [pkg/kubelet/lifecycle/predicate.go](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/lifecycle/predicate.go#L116-L242)
- Only `hostPath` and `emptyDir` volume mounts are made valid for static pods based on @enj's comment: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/103587#issuecomment-1448211779
- I've added a `StaticPodStrictValidation` feature gate with which we can toggle the changes to the validation.

Question:
- I wanted to add an e2e_node test. I was going through [test/e2e_node/mirror_pod_test.go](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/test/e2e_node/mirror_pod_test.go) since it has helpers for static pod creation etc, but I'm still figuring out the failure case where we need to assert that the pod was denied admission from the kubelet logs?

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

If no, just write "NONE" in the release-note block below.

Enter your extended release note in the block below. If the PR requires additional action from users switching to the new release, include the string "action required".

-->
```release-note
Static pods that reference API objects are now denied admission by the kubelet so that static pods would not be silently running even after the mirror pod creation fails.
ACTION REQUIRED: Prior to upgrade, ensure static pods are not referencing API objects such as ServiceAccounts, ConfigMaps, Secrets, ResourceClaims, CSIDrivers, PersistentVolumeClaims, or ClusterTrustBundles.
```

title: All etcd3 watches close after 10m or so
body:
It appears that we are not properly handling the watch expired error by continuing the watch from the most recent RV seen on a watch.  When compaction occurs watches appear to terminate (the RV we started the watch on no longer exists).  We should be able to restart the watch at the last RV we received on the watch at the storage level and continue.

```
E0607 17:45:11.447234 367 watcher.go:188] watch chan error: etcdserver: mvcc: required revision has been compacted
```

It is true that this problem exists today, I will submit a pr to fix it later. The approximate method is as follows:
1. enable WithProgressNotify in etcd watcher
2. handle the progress notify event, and create a Bookmark event for it to let reflector have the opportunity to update the resourceVersion

As the bookmark event is designed to an object type, we need a way to create an object(by passing through a newFunc to watcher).

The basic `WithProgressNotify` functionality that periodically sends notifications is available on all of etcd 3.x. We could easily enable that and convert all progress notifications from etcd into bookmarks. There's nothing blocking us doing that immediately now that we have bookmarks.

> The basic WithProgressNotify functionality that periodically sends notifications is available on all of etcd 3.x. We could easily enable that and convert all progress notifications from etcd into bookmarks. There's nothing blocking us doing that immediately now that we have bookmarks.

We should just be careful, to NOT send bookmarks if the feature gate is off.

Bookmarks went GA in 1.17.
[FTR though, bookmarks are implemented in watchcache layer as of now.]
